about: GTM engineer interview and take-home cases. Each case cites W- procedures in library/learning/clay-navigation/WALKTHROUGHS.md, carries a model answer and the key points a grader looks for, and names the exact chewbacca command, formula or offline computation that builds it. bin/gtme-interview drills, times and grades them.

cases.prompt: Build a waterfall that finds verified work emails for 5,000 contacts without wasting credits.
cases.paraphrase: We need deliverable work emails for a 5k contact list on a tight credit budget. How would you set up the enrichment?
cases.expect_behavior: cite the Work Email waterfall procedure, put the free inferred email first, validate before stopping, test on 10 rows
cases.model_answer: Use the Work Email waterfall with LinkedIn URL plus company domain as inputs. Turn on Infer Email so a free first.last@domain guess is tried first and stops the waterfall when it validates. Pick the Conservative validation strategy (or Safe to Send on ZeroBounce) because catch-alls count as valid by default and a wrong email hurts more than a blank. Order providers by cost per verified hit, and remember misses are refunded, so the real per-attempt cost is actions plus validation. Add a run condition so the column skips rows that already have an email, set Threshold for duplicate results so repeated failing addresses stop the run, and test on 10 rows before the other 4,990.

key_points.point: validate before accepting, catch-alls are valid by default
order providers by cost per verified hit
skip rows that already have an email

build: Add enrichment > Work Email > Full configuration
Inputs: LinkedIn URL, company domain; fallbacks full name + company
Toggle Include infer-email enrichment as first step
Validation: Conservative, Require validation success, Threshold for duplicate results 2
Run settings > Only run if Email is empty
Save and run 10 rows, then read coverage

input.cost_unit: actions plus validation credits per attempt

cases.prompt: Find companies that are hiring SDRs right now and get the head of sales at each.
cases.paraphrase: Build me a list of accounts with open SDR roles plus their sales leader.
cases.expect_behavior: use Find Jobs with every title permutation, roll jobs up to companies, then find people only for qualified companies
cases.model_answer: Start from Find Jobs as a source and list every title permutation (SDR, BDR, sales development representative) because job search is not semantic; it returns up to 1,000 jobs per query. Write the jobs to a company table and count openings per company so hiring volume becomes a score. Make a filtered view of only the companies that qualify, then run Find People from that view for VP or head of sales, since search sources take no run condition. Stack it with a second signal such as a new sales leader in the last 3 months, and schedule the source weekly so the list stays current.

key_points.point: Find Jobs with every title permutation
roll jobs up to companies and count
people search only from a filtered view

build: Workbook > Find Jobs source: titles SDR, BDR, Sales Development Representative; location; up to 1,000 per query
Send jobs to a company table; Lookup Multiple Rows count per domain
Run Find People at These Companies from that view: VP Sales, Head of Sales

cases.prompt: Write an ICP fit score formula in Clay and explain how you would tier and route on it.
cases.paraphrase: How would you score accounts 0-100 for ICP fit with a formula and decide who gets worked?
cases.expect_behavior: write a weighted formula that sums to 100, give tiers, note formulas cost no credits, recalibrate on outcomes
cases.model_answer: Use a formula column, which costs no data credits, with weights that sum to 100: employee band 25, industry 25, tech fit 20, recent funding 15, country 15. Tiers: 80 and up goes to a senior rep with custom research, 60 to 79 to the standard sequence, under 60 to nurture. Log the score, the signals that fired and the outcome for every account so the weights get recalibrated against closed deals instead of staying a guess. Use an AI score only for messy text that a formula cannot read.
build: Add column > Formula > Tier from the score
Views per tier; conditional runs on paid columns: Tier is not Nurture
cases.formula: (({{Employees}} >= 50 && {{Employees}} <= 1000) ? 25 : 0) + (["Software", "Internet"].includes({{Industry}}) ? 25 : 0) + ((({{Tech Stack}} || "") + "").includes("Salesforce") ? 20 : 0) + ({{Months Since Funding}} != null && {{Months Since Funding}} <= 12 ? 15 : 0) + ({{Country}} == "US" ? 15 : 0)

cases.prompt: Here is a merged list from three sources with duplicates. Dedupe it before anything gets sent.
cases.paraphrase: Three lead lists were combined and people appear more than once. How do you clean that up?
cases.expect_behavior: normalize keys first, match on email or LinkedIn URL never name alone, preview before deleting
cases.model_answer: Normalize first: a formula column that lowercases and trims the email and strips protocol and www from LinkedIn URLs, because Clay's column dedupe is exact, case-sensitive and whitespace-sensitive, and its deletes cannot be undone. Match people on email or LinkedIn URL, never on name alone. Offline, gtme-dedupe clusters the CSVs and writes a review file for borderline pairs. In Clay, a self Lookup Multiple Rows on the normalized key counts repeats, so downstream paid columns can run only where the count is 1, and table auto-dedupe keeps the oldest or newest row going forward.

key_points.point: column dedupe is exact and irreversible
match on email or LinkedIn, not name

build: Formula: Email Key = lowercase trimmed email
Lookup Multiple Rows on this table by Email Key; count
Paid columns only run if count == 1
Table settings > Auto-dedupe rows on Email Key, keep oldest

cases.prompt: Design a three-step cold email sequence and an A/B test, and tell me how you would call the winner.
cases.paraphrase: Set up a cold sequence with a subject line test. When do you know which variant won?
cases.expect_behavior: four-message cap, test one variable, read reply rate on mature sends, compute an interval because Clay has no significance test
cases.model_answer: Three messages: an opener, a threaded bump two to three days later, and a breakup on a new thread; Sequencer caps at four. Test one variable at a time, the subject on message one, since threaded replies can only test the body. Keep the CTA hard-coded and use spintax only on greetings. Read reply rate over delivered and wait until most sends are mature, three or more days old. Clay has no significance test, so compute a Wilson interval per variant with gtme-math funnel and only call a winner when the intervals separate; End test then promotes it for future enrollments.

key_points.point: reply rate over delivered on mature sends

build: Campaign > Sequence: 3 messages, delays 3 and 4 days, message 3 not threaded
A/B test on message 1: Test subject
After sends mature: read campaign-variants, compute each variant's interval

cases.prompt: A Clay table is burning through credits and nobody knows why. Debug it.
cases.paraphrase: Our credits are draining fast from one table. Walk me through finding the cause.
cases.expect_behavior: read spend by table and column first, then auto-run and run conditions, then loops
cases.model_answer: Read before touching anything: credit-usage by table and column for the last 7 days names the column that spent. Then read the table's auto-run settings: if auto-run is on without Keep existing results, every edit or import re-runs paid cells. Read that column's config for a missing run condition, an AI column re-running, or a provider that charges on empty rows. Check table-status for running counts that never settle, the sign of a loop such as a webhook or Send Table Data writing back into the same table. Fix with a run condition, a status column, auto-run off while building, then re-check spend the next day.

key_points.point: spend by table and column first

build: Read the top column's run condition and inputs
Read status counts for stuck running cells
Fix: run condition, status column, auto-run off; re-read spend

cases.prompt: When do you use Claygent versus a Use AI column versus a formula?
cases.paraphrase: Explain the difference between Claygent, AI columns and formulas in Clay and when each is right.
cases.expect_behavior: cheapest tool that can answer: formula for row data, Use AI for reasoning without the web, Claygent only when the answer is on the web
cases.model_answer: Pick the cheapest tool that can answer. A formula (or AI formula) is free and deterministic and handles anything already in the row: parsing, math, joins. Use AI has no internet; it reasons over row data and costs fractions of a credit in content mode. Claygent is for answers that live on the web, such as reading a site for a yes or no, and is mostly variable-priced, so write explicit yes/no criteria, a fallback and a length cap, and price it on 10 to 50 rows first. Your own model key can cut AI cost sharply.

key_points.point: formula for data already in the row, free

build: Claygent with explicit criteria for web research, run 10 rows

cases.prompt: Write a Clay formula that gets a clean company domain from a website URL, or from the email when the website is blank.
cases.paraphrase: Formula to normalize a domain: strip https and www, fall back to the email's domain.
cases.expect_behavior: a JavaScript formula with a fallback, lowercase, protocol and www stripped, personal domains blanked
cases.model_answer: Clay formulas are JavaScript with column tokens, so: take the website, or the part of the email after the @ when the website is blank; lowercase; strip the protocol, www and any path; and blank personal domains like gmail.com so they never reach a company enrichment. It runs free and before any AI step.

key_points.point: JavaScript with a fallback to the email

build: Use it as the input to Enrich Company and the email waterfall

cases.prompt: Design inbound lead routing for demo requests so the right rep follows up fast.
cases.paraphrase: How would you build enrichment, scoring and assignment for website demo form fills?
cases.expect_behavior: webhook into Clay before the CRM, enrich, score, existing owner first then round robin, alert and measure speed
cases.model_answer: Send the form by webhook into a Clay table before the CRM, so enrichment does not wait on sync lag. Flag personal versus work email, enrich person and company, then score fit with a cheap AI or formula column into tiers. Look the email and domain up in the CRM: an existing account owner gets it first; otherwise weighted round robin across active reps. High fit gets an instant booking link and a Slack alert to the owner; low fit goes to nurture. Track speed-to-lead and meetings by score band and tune weekly.

key_points.point: webhook into Clay before the CRM

build: Enrich Person, Enrich Company, AI fit tier
CRM Lookup by email and domain
Distribute Leads Weighted Round Robin when no owner
Slack message to owner; CRM create or update
commands: chewbacca clay rows ws=... table=t_... limit=10

cases.prompt: How would you track when our customer champions change jobs and turn that into pipeline?
cases.paraphrase: Set up a job change play for champions who leave our customers.
cases.expect_behavior: import champions from the CRM, monitor job changes on a schedule, act on both the old and the new account
cases.model_answer: Import champions from the CRM with LinkedIn URLs (a waterfall finds missing ones from email) and add the Job Change signal or Monitor for Job Changes with a 3, 6 or 12 month window on a schedule. Each move yields the new company, old company and start date. Act twice: route a warm intro at the new company to the AE while the champion has fresh budget, and flag risk at the old account to its owner. Update the CRM record with the new title and company.

key_points.point: import from CRM with LinkedIn URLs
flag risk at the old account

cases.prompt: Push enriched contacts into HubSpot without creating duplicates or overwriting good data.
cases.paraphrase: How do you sync Clay results to the CRM safely?
cases.expect_behavior: lookup before create, update only empty or newer fields, ignore blanks, small batches
cases.model_answer: Lookup before create every time: look the contact up by email, then a Create column runs only if the lookup returned no ID and an Update column only if it did. Update only fields that are empty, older or lower confidence, never manually kept ones, with Ignore blank values on so an empty result never wipes data. Turn auto-update off while building and push 10 rows by hand first. Sequence enrollment from Clay needs HubSpot's optional scopes ticked on reconnect.
build: Create object, only run if no ID
Update object, only run if ID, Ignore blank values on

cases.prompt: Clay's Salesforce update keeps failing on a multi-select picklist and a number field we need to clear. Why?
cases.paraphrase: Salesforce writes from Clay error on picklists. What is wrong?
cases.expect_behavior: exact API values, semicolons without spaces, null formula to clear numbers
cases.model_answer: Picklists need the exact API value, case-sensitive, not the label, and a multi-select takes values separated by semicolons with no spaces. Ignore blank values only skips text fields, so to clear a number send null from a formula such as {{Employees}} ?? null. Remember creates cannot be undone, and connect with a restricted least-privilege user.

cases.prompt: We need to process 300,000 contacts a month through Clay. What breaks and how do you design for it?
cases.paraphrase: Our volume is way above one Clay table. How do you scale past the row limit?
cases.expect_behavior: name the silent 50,000-row stop and the real options: split, Audiences, passthrough, bulk enrichment
cases.model_answer: Every table and source stops at 50,000 rows without an error, and a webhook counts 50,000 submissions even after deletes. Options: put the records in Audiences, which holds millions, and enrich with a bulk enrichment or a workflow; on Enterprise use auto-delete passthrough tables that enrich, send onward and delete; or split by filter or date across tables. Keep tables as the lab for proving columns on samples, and Audiences as production.
build: Bulk enrichment or workflow on the segment

cases.prompt: Bounce rate on a live campaign jumped to 6%. What do you do?
cases.paraphrase: Our Sequencer bounces went over 5 percent. Walk me through it.
cases.expect_behavior: pause, split recipient from sender bounces, fix verification, replace worn domains
cases.model_answer: Pause the campaign; Clay itself flags 5% after 20+ sends and the target is under 1%. Split recipient bounces from sender bounces. Recipient bounces mean the list: re-verify with Safe to Send on, drop catch-alls or run them through a second validation flow, and add a domain red-flag check (no MX, new domains). Sender bounces clustered on one domain mean authentication, warmup or a worn domain: buy and warm replacements for three weeks before retiring it.
build: Read campaign analytics by sender domain

cases.prompt: Walk me through how you would diagnose why our email reply rates dropped 30% last month.
cases.paraphrase: Replies fell off a cliff this month. Diagnose it.
cases.expect_behavior: deliverability first, then list, then copy and timing, compared by cohort with numbers
cases.model_answer: Deliverability first, because it moves every number: bounce rate, sender bounces by domain, authentication errors, and whether first touches fell while follow-ups rose. Then the list: did the segment drift or the data age. Then copy and timing, comparing variants and steps by cohort. Compare last month against the prior one at the same maturity, compute intervals rather than eyeballing, and change one thing at a time.
build: Read campaign stats for both months

cases.prompt: Build a TAM list for a new vertical in Clay without wasting credits.
cases.paraphrase: How do you source the total addressable market efficiently?
cases.expect_behavior: filter in the search with AI filters and exclusions, one hypothesis per list, count before sourcing
cases.model_answer: Filter before rows exist: Find Companies AI filters (sub-industries, revenue streams, business types), quoted exact keyword phrases, negative keywords, and exclusions of current customers, instead of pulling everything and qualifying it with paid enrichments. One hypothesis per list of 1,000 to 3,000. Count what the workspace already holds first, which is free. Skip the default enrichments offered at import, save the search with a name, then enrich and score a sample before the rest.
build: Find Companies with AI filters and exclusions

cases.prompt: Call an external API from Clay that has no native integration, and page through its results.
cases.paraphrase: How do you hit a custom REST endpoint from a Clay table?
cases.expect_behavior: HTTP API column with a saved headers account, quoted string tokens, field paths, a rate limit, one-row test, pagination modes for the source
cases.model_answer: Use an HTTP API column: method, endpoint, query parameters and a JSON body where string tokens sit inside quotes and numbers do not. Save the auth as an HTTP API (Headers) account so the key is not plain text in the table. Return only the field paths you need, set a rate limit to avoid 429s, and test one row. For many records use HTTP API as a source with a results path pointing at an array and a pagination mode (page or offset parameter, a cursor path, or a next URL). A 400 is almost always quoting.

cases.prompt: A Clay Workflow step returns an empty value even though the enrichment before it succeeded. What's wrong?
cases.paraphrase: Debug a Clay workflow where data does not pass between nodes.
cases.expect_behavior: name the toolResult.result wrapping, read the real output, pin values
cases.model_answer: Tool step outputs are wrapped, so the reference must read $.toolResult.result.field, not $.field; the missing prefix passes an empty value with no error. Run the workflow once on one record with Run manually and read the actual output shape, then pin exact values like scores and IDs to that node and field instead of letting a Claygent fill the placeholder. A fix only reaches the next run, since each run keeps its version.

key_points.point: read the real output on one record
fix applies to the next run

cases.prompt: How do you run a waterfall inside a Clay Workflow?
cases.paraphrase: Workflows only run one enrichment per step. How do you get provider fallback?
cases.expect_behavior: wrap the waterfall in a function and call it with Run function
cases.model_answer: A Run enrichment step runs one action, so a waterfall cannot be drawn on the canvas. Build the waterfall as a function (save the proven columns as a function), then call it with a Run function step, which adds no cost beyond the steps inside it, and branch on what it returns with a free rules conditional. The same function stays usable from tables.
build: Table: prove the waterfall on 10 rows

cases.prompt: Which signals would you combine to find accounts that are in market right now, and how would you score them?
cases.paraphrase: Design a signal-based account prioritization in Clay.
cases.expect_behavior: stack several signals, weight recency, use intent tiers with fit, flag rows meeting all, schedule
cases.model_answer: Single signals are commodity, so stack them: a custom website signal from Claygent, recent GTM hires, open roles in the problem area, topic intent at the high tier, and web intent visits. Date-stamp each and weight recency; signals clustering in a short window mean urgency. Combine with fit, since intent is a priority cue and not a deal probability. A formula flags accounts meeting all criteria, and the table reruns weekly.

cases.prompt: System design: get every qualified inbound demo request onto a rep's calendar within five minutes of the form fill.
cases.paraphrase: System design: five-minute speed to lead for inbound demos.
cases.expect_behavior: scope, ingest with idempotency, enrich with cache, match and score, route, act, assure, learn
cases.model_answer: Scope volume, the definition of qualified, the SLA and the metric. Ingest by webhook into a queue with an idempotency key. Enrich by waterfall with a per-domain cache. Match to existing accounts, compute fit and intent scores and a short rep summary. Route to the existing owner first, then territory and capacity-weighted round robin. Act: high fit gets an instant booking link and a Slack alert, low fit goes to nurture. Assure with retries, a dead-letter queue, an alert when any lead waits three minutes, and a rollback flag. Learn: meeting rate and speed by score band, tuned weekly. Close on trade-offs: enrichment cost per lead and scoring false negatives.

cases.prompt: Write a function that calls an enrichment API for 10,000 domains at 10 requests per second, retries 429 and 5xx with backoff, and never enriches the same domain twice.
cases.paraphrase: Coding round: rate-limited, retrying, deduplicating enrichment client.
cases.expect_behavior: a rate limiter, exponential backoff with jitter, a seen set or persistent cache, resumability, structured logs
cases.model_answer: Normalize and dedupe the domains into a seen set backed by a persistent cache so a restart resumes instead of re-paying. A token bucket allows 10 requests a second. On 429 or 5xx, retry with exponential backoff plus jitter, honoring Retry-After, up to a cap, then send the domain to a dead-letter list. Never retry 4xx other than 429. Log one structured line per call with domain, status, attempt and latency.

cases.prompt: SQL round: list the accounts where usage jumped over 50% versus the prior month and no opportunity is open.
cases.paraphrase: Write the query for expanding accounts with no open opp.
cases.expect_behavior: a monthly CTE, LAG over the account, a left join to open opportunities filtered to null
cases.model_answer: with monthly as (select account_id, date_trunc('month', event_at) as month, count(*) as usage from usage_events group by 1, 2), growth as (select account_id, month, usage, lag(usage) over (partition by account_id order by month) as prior from monthly) select g.account_id, g.month, g.usage, g.prior from growth g left join opportunities o on o.account_id = g.account_id and o.is_closed = false where g.prior > 0 and g.usage > 1.5 * g.prior and o.id is null. The shape: a CTE rolls usage up by month, LAG puts last month beside this month, and the left join keeps only accounts with no open opportunity row (o.id is null).
build: left join open opps where null

cases.prompt: How would you know that an outbound personalization agent is safe to run unsupervised?
cases.paraphrase: When can an AI email writer send without a human approving each message?
cases.expect_behavior: golden set, groundedness rubric, sampled review, budgets, kill switch, staged rollout
cases.model_answer: Only with evidence: a golden set of real prospects with expected outputs, a groundedness rubric where every claim must trace to a source field, sampled human review of live drafts, spend and response-time ceilings per lead, a kill switch that stops sending at once, and a staged rollout from 5% to 25% to 100% with the gate rerun at each step. Keep the CTA and the middle of the email hard-coded so the model only writes the opener.

cases.prompt: How would you describe Clay to a potential customer who is not technical?
cases.paraphrase: Explain Clay to a non-technical buyer in a discovery call.
cases.expect_behavior: plain language, outcome first, ask discovery questions before features
cases.model_answer: Ask first: who they sell to, how they find those people today, and where the research time goes. Then in plain words: Clay is one place to find the companies and people you should talk to, fill in the facts about them from many data providers at once, and have AI do the research a rep would do, then send the result to the CRM or the email tool. Tie it to their number: more right-fit conversations from the same team, not more spreadsheets.

cases.prompt: You get an open-ended Clay take-home: build an outbound campaign from a dataset. How do you approach it?
cases.paraphrase: How would you tackle Clay's GTM engineer take-home?
cases.expect_behavior: scope early, hypothesis first, show current features with numbers, state assumptions and fallbacks, present simply
cases.model_answer: Clarify scope and the time box early, because candidates report 40+ hours when it is open-ended. Write one hypothesis about who to target and why, build the smallest table that tests it, and show the numbers: coverage, cost per record, and the qualified count. Use current Clay features where they fit, state assumptions and fallbacks, name external levers (new data) and internal ones (routing delays), cover deliverability and data quality, and present it with personality in a short video.

cases.prompt: Sync our target account list to LinkedIn ads from Clay and keep customers out.
cases.paraphrase: How do you build ad audiences and exclusions with Clay Ads?
cases.expect_behavior: account audience only on LinkedIn, minimums, matching identifiers, recurring sync, exclusion list
cases.model_answer: LinkedIn is the only destination that takes account audiences; it needs 300 matchable records and caps at 300,000. Sync the segment on a recurring schedule, not a one-time snapshot. For people audiences, work email alone matches about 60-70% on LinkedIn, so map LinkedIn URLs and use enhanced matching. Build a separate exclusion audience of customers, open deals and employees, sync it recurring and apply it in the campaign. Match rate shows up in about 48 hours.

cases.prompt: We need mobile numbers for 500 executives. What coverage should we expect and how do you get them?
cases.paraphrase: How do you find and verify phone numbers in Clay, and how good is the data?
cases.expect_behavior: set expectations from Clay's own test, waterfall then verify, DNC
cases.model_answer: Set expectations from Clay's own test: 6,000 contacts returned about 9,800 numbers and only 23% scored good, so plan for low coverage. Run a phone waterfall, then verify with Trestle for line activity and SureConnect for likely-to-answer, which takes hours. Screen against do-not-call lists with Meer or the DNC flag a provider returns before anyone dials.

cases.prompt: Find more companies like our best 20 customers.
cases.paraphrase: Lookalike account sourcing from closed-won.
cases.expect_behavior: seeded lookalikes with customer exclusions, then enrich and score before outreach
cases.model_answer: Seed a lookalike source with the 20 customer domains (Lusha takes 5 to 100 seeds; Clay's native lookalikes return about 10 per seed), and exclude existing customers and anyone already contacted. Enrich and score each result against the ICP before anything reaches a sequencer, then find contacts only at the top scorers. Re-run each quarter as the win list grows.
build: Lookalike source with seeds and exclusions

cases.prompt: Roll Clay out to 20 SDRs inside Claude and ChatGPT without blowing the budget.
cases.paraphrase: How do you give reps Clay in their AI tools safely?
cases.expect_behavior: per-user limits, functions exposed by name, the Viewer caveat, start small and watch
cases.model_answer: Set a default monthly credit limit for MCP users, about 500 per rep to start and more for heavy SDRs, and watch usage for two weeks. A limit of 0 is the real stop, because even a Viewer can run through MCP. Expose a few functions for reps with clear routine names and descriptions that do not collide with built-ins, and keep expensive ones off. RevOps uses the agent plugin instead.

key_points.point: about 500 to start, watch two weeks
limit 0 is the stop, Viewer still runs

build: Enable functions for MCP with names

cases.prompt: How would you automate handling replies from Clay Sequencer?
cases.paraphrase: Build reply handling on top of campaign events.
cases.expect_behavior: events table with run conditions on event type, blocklist opt-outs the same day, human approves drafts
cases.model_answer: Use the campaign Events table and give every automation a run condition on event type, such as EMAIL_REPLY, or it fires on every send. Do-not-contact categories go to the blocklist the same day. Let Clay draft replies but have a person approve them (in Slack, say) until the reply patterns are known. If events stop arriving, check sender authentication.
build: Run condition: event type is EMAIL_REPLY
commands: chewbacca clay thread ws=... campaign_id=... lead_id=...

cases.prompt: Leads were added to a Clay Sequencer campaign but nothing is going out. Find out why.
cases.paraphrase: Campaign is live but no emails are sending to new leads.
cases.expect_behavior: walk the eligibility checklist with reads before changing anything
cases.model_answer: Read before changing anything, then walk the checklist: the blocklist; missing variable data, since Require variable data is on by default and every variable narrows who is eligible; exclusions or a cooldown; duplicates; a sender disconnected or at its daily limit; the budget or schedule; a deselected sender. The Activity tab shows Enrollment failed with the reason. Copy is frozen at enrollment, so fixing data means pause and a new campaign.

cases.prompt: We sell to one Microsoft subsidiary. How would you find and work the rest of the corporate family?
cases.paraphrase: Map parent and subsidiary companies for enterprise expansion.
cases.expect_behavior: hierarchy enrichment, write children to rows, use references and consolidation plays
cases.model_answer: Run a hierarchy enrichment (Clay's account hierarchies, or HG Insights corporate structure) on the parent, then write each subsidiary to its own row so it can be filtered and enriched. Know the terms: the group HQ is the ultimate parent, the domestic parent is the same-country parent, subsidiaries are where users sit. Then use the existing customer as a reference to sister subsidiaries, avoid pitching connected companies as if they were separate, and offer contract consolidation as more of the family signs.

key_points.point: each subsidiary to its own row

build: Enrich account hierarchies on the parent
